cases.reason: The rule leans on the term zero-length item. §2002:8.5.4 lists five cases; each has a 2023 counterpart in §2023:8.5.4 (variable-occurrence item vs occurs-depending table: 2002's only variable-occurrence form is OCCURS DEPENDING, §2002:4.187; ANY LENGTH; logical record of zero characters; intrinsic function), 2023 only adding cases (DYNAMIC LENGTH, dynamic-capacity tables, zero-length literals, ref-mod). No 2002 case is outside 2023's list, and the statically detectable one is refused at 2002 by the SR5 arm (pb177, COBOL1699). A CD record cannot be zero-length (fixed record description).

cases.reason: Format and rules of 13.16.19 are identical to 13.18.21; in 2002 ERASE/EOL/EOS occur only in a screen description entry (2002 8.9 table). The 2002 text licenses non-support on its own terms: the screen section is a processor-dependent element (§2002:B.3 item 1) and §2002:3.1.5 lets an unclaimed one go unimplemented, requiring a compile-time warning and a statement of absence in user documentation (docs/conformance/5/A.4.2.md). The twin's witness uses only ERASE END OF LINE, so I probed the EOL and EOS spellings: refused at --std 2002 with COBOL1560 at the section header and the clause, exit 65.
